title: French
description: Everyday French: greetings, family, food, numbers, getting around and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: Use 'bonjour' during the day and 'bonsoir' in the evening. 'Salut' (hi, bye) is informal: keep it for friends.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: Every noun is masculine or feminine: 'le père' (the father), 'la mère' (the mother). Before a vowel, 'le' and 'la' become l': l'enfant.

phrases.t: Ma mère est à la maison.

teach.t: Ma mère est à la maison.

exercises.prompt: Ma mère est à la maison.

answers: Ma mère est à la maison.

exercises.text: Ma mère est à la maison.
answers: Ma mère est à la maison.

units.title: Food and drink
tips: 'Du', 'de la' and 'de l'' mean 'some': 'je bois du café'. After 'ne ... pas' they become 'de': 'je ne bois pas de lait'.

phrases.t: Je ne bois pas de lait.

teach.t: Je ne bois pas de lait.

exercises.prompt: Je ne bois pas de lait.

answers: Je ne bois pas de lait.

exercises.text: Je ne bois pas de lait.
answers: Je ne bois pas de lait.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: 'Combien ?' means 'how much?' or 'how many?'. For the time, use 'Il est ... heures': 'Il est trois heures'.

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: 'Où est ... ?' means 'Where is ...?'. 'Les toilettes' is always plural in French.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: Days of the week are not capitalised in French: lundi, mardi, mercredi...

units.title: Shopping
units.description: Ask for things, prices and how to pay.
tips: Ask for something with "je voudrais" (I would like): it is politer than "je veux" (I want).

alts: Est-ce que le magasin est ouvert ?
Est-ce que je peux payer par carte ?
